mainTopic: The end of the משנה on altered שופרות, echoes, and כוונה, and the גמרא's rulings on changes to a שופר (plating, patches, cracks, inverting, drilling) and on blowing into a pit.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה and then begins the גמרא on it. The משנה rules that a patched hole disqualifies a שופר only if it blocks the blowing. It also rules that blowing into a pit counts only if the real sound is heard and not an echo, and that someone who hears the שופר or the מגילה from outside the בית הכנסת is יוצא only with כוונה. The גמרא brings two ברייתות about altered שופרות: shortening and scraping are fine, gold plating depends on where it is and whether it changes the sound, and a שופר inside a שופר depends on which sound is heard. רב פפא explains that an 'inverted' שופר means one whose wide and narrow ends were reversed. It is פסול because of רב מתנה's reading of ״והעברת״. On glued fragments and patches, the תנא קמא and רבי נתן disagree, and רבי יוחנן's limit on רבי נתן is given in two versions. A crack is judged by its direction, and the minimum blowing length is set by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A drilled-through bony core is not a barrier, because it is מין במינו. Finally, רב הונא explains that the pit case fails only for listeners at the edge, and a ברייתא confirms this in two versions. The amud ends as רבה begins a new statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A punctured שופר that was sealed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a sealed hole makes the שופר פסול only if the patch interferes with the blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a שופר got a hole and someone sealed it: if the patch interferes with the blowing, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule about a שופר that had a hole and was patched up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A patch does not automatically ruin a שופר. The test is practical: does the patch get in the way of the תקיעה? If it does, the שופר is פסול. If it does not, it stays כשר.

phrases.english: If it was punctured and he sealed it,
if it impedes the blowing, it is unfit,
and if not, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of damaged-שופר rules on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed hole is פסול only if the patch interferes with the תקיעה. Otherwise the שופר is כשר.

steps.title: Blowing into a pit or a large jar
steps.stepSummary: Someone who blows into a hollow space is יוצא only if the listener heard the real שופר sound and not an echo.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone blows into a pit, a cistern, or a big jar: if he heard the sound of the שופר, he is יוצא. If he heard an echo, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from damage to the שופר itself to a problem with where the sound is heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hollow places make sound bounce back as an echo. The מצוה is to hear the actual שופר sound, so an echo does not count. Everything depends on which sound reached the listener.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern (a walled pit for water)
An echo, a distorted reverberating sound

steps.confusionAlert: There is nothing wrong with the שופר here. The problem is only what the listener actually heard: the real sound or a bounced-back echo.

phrases.english: One who blows into a pit
or into a cistern
or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the shofar, he fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שָׁמַע — לָא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of an echo, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the physical condition of the שופר to the quality of the sound the listener hears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the real שופר sound counts. An echo does not.

steps.title: Hearing from outside the synagogue requires intent
steps.stepSummary: A person who hears the שופר or the מגילה from outside the בית הכנסת is יוצא only if he had כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, someone walking behind a בית הכנסת, or whose house is next to it, who heard the שופר or the מגילה: if he had in mind to fulfill the מצוה, he is יוצא. If not, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new requirement: besides hearing the right sound, the listener must have כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the issue was whether the sound itself was valid. Here the sound is perfectly valid, yet the person can still miss the מצוה. The deciding factor is his inner intent to fulfill the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: The sound of the מגילה (מגילת אסתר) being read
He focused his heart, meaning he had intent to fulfill the מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a key source for the principle that מצוות need כוונה, a topic the גמרא develops at length.

phrases.english: And similarly, one who was passing
behind a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or whose house was adjacent to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of the shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he focused his heart, he fulfilled his obligation,
and if not, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The word וכן links this case to the previous one: in both, hearing alone is not automatically enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing a valid שופר or מגילה counts only if the listener had כוונה to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Two people hear the same sound, but only one is יוצא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: two people can hear the identical sound, yet only the one with כוונה fulfills the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though this one heard and that one heard, this one had intent and that one did not have intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a summary line that makes the previous rule vivid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two people are identical on the outside, since both heard the same sound. The only difference between them is internal. This shows that כוונה, not just the physical act of hearing, decides whether the מצוה was done.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three tests for hearing שופר: the שופר must not be ruined (for example, by a patch that blocks the blowing), the sound must be real and not an echo, and the listener must have כוונה.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה שָׁמַע וְזֶה שָׁמַע,
phrases.english: Even though this one heard and that one heard,
this one focused his heart,
and that one did not focus his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה שָׁמַע וְזֶה שָׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes and sharpens the כוונה rule from step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The same sound can fulfill the מצוה for one person and not for another. The difference is כוונה.

steps.title: A shortened or thinly scraped שופר is still fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: a שופר that was shortened, or scraped down to a thin layer, is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a long שופר that was shortened is fit. If it was scraped until only a thin layer was left, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא with more rules about changes to a שופר. This ברייתא sets up the list that continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing material from the שופר, whether by cutting it shorter or scraping it thin, does not ruin it. It is still the same horn, so it stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and analyzes the משנה
The Sages taught, introducing a ברייתא
He left it down to its thin outer layer

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
If it was long and he shortened it, it is fit.
If he scraped it and left it down to its thin layer, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins, bringing a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's rules about altered שופרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shortening or thinning a שופר does not make it פסול.

steps.title: Gold plating where the mouth goes
steps.stepSummary: Gold plating at the mouthpiece makes the שופר פסול. Gold plating elsewhere does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he plated it with gold at the place where the mouth goes, it is unfit. If not at the place where the mouth goes, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and now deals with adding gold to the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location of the gold matters. At the mouthpiece, the person would be blowing through gold instead of through the שופר itself, so it is פסול. Gold placed elsewhere does not touch the blowing, so the שופר stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where one puts his mouth (the mouthpiece)

phrases.aramaic: צִיפָּהוּ זָהָב בִּמְקוֹם הַנָּחַת פֶּה — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he plated it with gold at the place where the mouth is placed, it is unfit.
If not at the place where the mouth is placed, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from removing material from the שופר to adding material onto it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold at the mouthpiece makes the שופר פסול. Gold elsewhere does not.

steps.title: Gold plating inside versus outside
steps.stepSummary: Gold plating inside the שופר always makes it פסול. Gold plating outside makes it פסול only if it changed the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he plated it with gold on the inside, it is unfit. On the outside: if its sound changed from what it was, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second gold-plating rule, this time comparing the inside of the שופר to the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold on the inside means the sound travels through gold, so it is not a pure שופר sound, and it is פסול no matter what. Gold on the outside is just decoration, so it is פסול only if it actually changed how the שופר sounds.
steps.confusionAlert: The sound test applies only to outside plating. Inside plating is פסול even if the sound seems unchanged.

phrases.english: If he plated it with gold on the inside, it is unfit.
On the outside:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נִשְׁתַּנָּה קוֹלוֹ מִכְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: if its sound changed from how it was, it is unfit,
and if not, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the gold-plating rules, now distinguishing inside from outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside plating is always פסול. Outside plating is פסול only if it changed the sound.

steps.title: The ברייתא repeats the sealed-hole rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא includes the same sealed-hole rule that appeared in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was punctured and he sealed it: if it impedes the blowing, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule about a patched hole as part of its own list. The גמרא will soon analyze this rule more closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as in the משנה, but here it appears inside the ברייתא's larger list of altered שופרות. Because the ruling is simply restated, it becomes the starting point for the גמרא's upcoming questions about what kind of patch is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: If it was punctured and he sealed it,
if it impedes the blowing, it is unfit,
and if not, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues its list and restates the rule from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed hole is פסול only if the patch interferes with the תקיעה.

steps.title: One שופר placed inside another
steps.stepSummary: When one שופר is placed inside another, he is יוצא only if the sound heard came from the inner שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put a שופר inside a שופר: if he heard the sound of the inner one, he is יוצא. If he heard the sound of the outer one, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends this list with a case of two שופרות nested one inside the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sound heard is the inner שופר's own sound, it counts as blowing one שופר. If the sound that comes out is that of the outer שופר, it is a sound produced through two שופרות together, which is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The sound of the inner one
The sound of the outer one

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rules share one idea: a שופר stays כשר as long as the sound heard is the real sound of a single שופר. Shortening it, thinning it, or outside decoration that does not change the sound are all fine. Blowing through gold, a patch that blocks the blowing, or a sound produced through two שופרות make it פסול.

phrases.english: If he placed a shofar inside a shofar,
if he heard the sound of the inner one, he fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל חִיצוֹן שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of the outer one, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final case in the ברייתא's list of altered שופרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the inner שופר's own sound counts. A sound produced through both שופרות does not.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: scraping and a שופר inside a שופר
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא rules that scraping a שופר, inside or outside, even down to a thin layer, leaves it כשר. When one שופר is inside another, it depends on which sound was heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he scraped a שופר, whether inside or outside, it is כשר. If he scraped it down to its thin outer layer, it is still כשר. If he put one שופר inside another: if he heard the inner שופר's sound, he is יוצא. If he heard the outer one's sound, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא. Its first rulings are similar to things we already saw: scraping is fine, and in the case of a שופר inside a שופר, the sound must come from the inner one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different ברייתא from the one in steps 5 to 9, so the repeated rulings are not a mistake. What is new here is the detail 'בין מבפנים בין מבחוץ': scraping on either side is fine, because the שופר stays the same object. This ברייתא is leading up to its new case, the inverted שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: he scraped it (shaved down the horn)
from the inside / from the outside
its thin outer layer or skin
the sound of the inner שופר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is repeating itself by mistake. Some of these rulings appeared in steps 5 and 9, but this is a separate ברייתא that also contains a new case, the inverted שופר.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּרְדוֹ, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: If he scraped it, whether inside or outside, it is fit.
If he scraped it down to its thin layer, it is fit.
If he placed a shofar inside a shofar,
if he heard the inner sound, he fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל חִיצוֹן שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and if he heard the outer sound, he did not fulfill it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּרְדוֹ, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ — כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second ברייתא that overlaps with the earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scraping on either side, even down to a thin layer, does not make a שופר פסול. With a שופר inside a שופר, he is יוצא only from the inner sound.

steps.title: An inverted שופר does not work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a new case: if he turned the שופר over and blew it, he is not יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he turned it over and blew it, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a new ruling: a שופר that was 'turned over' cannot be used. This sets up רב פפא's explanation of what 'turned over' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הפכו is unclear. It could mean flipping the horn inside out, or reversing which end is wide and which is narrow. The ruling is clear (he is not יוצא), but the case still needs to be defined.

keyTerms.meaning: he turned it over or reversed it

phrases.english: If he inverted it and blew it, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with its new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inverted שופר is פסול.

steps.title: רב פפא defines what inverted means
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'inverted' does not mean turned inside out like a shirt. It means the narrow end was widened and the wide end was narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Don't say it means he turned it inside out like a shirt. Rather, it means he widened the narrow end and narrowed the wide end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the ברייתא's word הפכו so we know exactly which case is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might picture softening the horn and flipping it inside out. רב פפא says the case is different: the shape was reversed, so the person now blows into what used to be the wide end. This is a definition of the case, not a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: do not say (do not understand it this way)
like a shirt or tunic (turned inside out)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say that he turned it inside out like a tunic,
rather, that he widened the narrow end
and narrowed the wide end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Inverted' means the wide and narrow ends were reversed.

steps.title: Why is a reversed שופר unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason a reversed שופר is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why reversing the ends makes a שופר פסול. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is still the same horn and it still makes a sound, so the problem is not obvious. The גמרא wants a source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב פפא's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why a reversed שופר is פסול.

steps.title: רב מתנה's verse: blow it the way it grew
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows רב מתנה, who learns from ״והעברת״ that the שופר must be used in the same direction it grew on the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב מתנה, who said: The verse says ״והעברת״. We need the שופר the way it 'passes' (grows) on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a reversed שופר is פסול because of רב מתנה's reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״והעברת״ is connected to the root of העברה, the way the horn 'passed' along the animal's head. The שופר must keep its natural direction: narrow where it was narrow, wide where it was wide. Reversing the ends breaks that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you shall sound' (ויקרא כ״ה:ט), read as hinting to the horn's natural path
the way it passed (grew) on the animal

steps.whatToRemember: A שופר must be blown in its natural direction, the way it grew. Scraping is fine, but reversing the ends is פסול.

phrases.english: It is like Rav Mattana.
For Rav Mattana said:
"You shall sound [veha'avarta]": we require the way it was carried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״והעברת״ requires the שופר to be used in its natural direction.

steps.title: The משנה: glued שופר fragments are unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a שופר made by gluing broken pieces together is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he glued together broken pieces of שופרות, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. Quoting it sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שופר built from fragments is not one natural horn. This is the starting point for the discussion of added material and patches.

phrases.english: If he glued together broken fragments of shofarot, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שופר glued together from fragments is פסול.

steps.title: ברייתא: any addition or sealed hole disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that adding any amount of material, or sealing a hole, makes the שופר פסול, whether the material is horn or something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he added anything at all to it, whether horn or another material, it is פסול. If it got a hole and he sealed it, whether with horn or another material, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה. Even a small addition or patch disqualifies the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (the first opinion, the תנא קמא) is strict in both cases. It makes no difference whether the added material is the same kind as the שופר. Any foreign part means it is no longer a pure, natural horn.

keyTerms.meaning: it was punctured and he sealed it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he added anything at all to it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: whether of its kind or not of its kind, it is unfit.
If it was punctured and he sealed it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: whether with its kind or not with its kind, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוֹסִיף עָלָיו כׇּל שֶׁהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's ruling about glued fragments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any addition or patched hole makes a שופר פסול, regardless of the material.

steps.title: רבי נתן permits a patch of horn
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees: sealing a hole with horn is כשר, but sealing it with another material is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: With its own kind, it is כשר. Not with its own kind, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן disagrees with the first opinion about the case of a sealed hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, a horn patch blends in with the שופר, so it is still a horn. A different material is a foreign part. His disagreement is about the sealed hole.

keyTerms.meaning: not of its own kind (a foreign material)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
with its kind, it is fit;
not with its kind, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole sealed with horn is כשר. A hole sealed with another material is פסול.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי נתן's leniency applies only when most of the original שופר remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'with its own kind, it is כשר', רבי יוחנן said: That is only when most of the שופר remains.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a condition to רבי נתן's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horn patch is acceptable only if it is a small repair, so that most of the original horn is still intact. If the patching makes up most of the שופר, even רבי נתן agrees it is פסול.

phrases.english: "With its kind, it is fit":
Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is only where most of it remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִינוֹ כָּשֵׁר — אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי נתן's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A horn patch is כשר only if most of the original שופר is intact.

steps.title: Inference: a foreign patch is always unfit
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's words, the גמרא infers that a patch of another material is פסול even when most of the שופר remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can infer from this that with a different material, even if most of the שופר remains, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the 'most remains' condition only for a horn patch. This shows that 'most remains' does not help a patch of another material. A foreign material disqualifies the שופר in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference (we can conclude from this)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נתן as explained by רבי יוחנן: a horn patch is כשר only if most of the שופר remains, while a patch of another material is always פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets clear limits for practical cases of a שופר that was damaged and then repaired.

phrases.english: By inference, that not with its kind,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר רוּבּוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: even if most of it remained, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers the law for a foreign patch from רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A patch of another material makes a שופר פסול even when most of the original remains.

steps.title: A second version: רבי יוחנן's comment goes on the last clause
steps.stepSummary: Some attach רבי יוחנן's statement to the ruling that a patch of another material is פסול. In this version, it is פסול only when most of the שופר was missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the last clause. 'With a different material, it is פסול.' רבי יוחנן said: that is only when most of it was missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of where רבי יוחנן's comment was said. In this version, he was limiting the strict ruling about patching with a different material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי יוחנן limited the leniency: a patch of the same material is כשר only if most of the שופר remains. In this version, he limits the strictness instead: a patch of another material is פסול only when most of the שופר was missing. So the same words now point in the lenient direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it this way (an alternate version)
The last clause of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In version one, רבי יוחנן's words make the rule stricter. In version two, the same words make it more lenient.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the last clause:
If it was sealed with a different material, it is unfit,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
That is only when most of it was missing.
phrases.notes: In that case the foreign patch makes up most of the שופר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different placement of רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A patch of another material makes the שופר פסול only when most of the original שופר was missing.

steps.title: Inference: a same-material patch is כשר even if most is missing
steps.stepSummary: From the second version, the גמרא infers that a patch of the same material is כשר even when most of the שופר was missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows that with the same material, even if most of it was missing, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a logical conclusion from the second version of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limited the strictness to a foreign patch, and only when most was missing. That implies a same-material patch is never a problem, even when it makes up most of the שופר. This is the reverse of the inference in Step 19.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי יוחנן. Version 1: a same-material patch is כשר only if most of the שופר remains, and a foreign patch is always פסול. Version 2: a same-material patch is always כשר, and a foreign patch is פסול only if most of the שופר was missing.

phrases.english: By inference, with the same material,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּפְחַת רוּבּוֹ — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: even if most of it was missing, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the implication of Step 20, the counterpart to Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the second version, a same-material patch is כשר even if it makes up most of the שופר.

steps.title: A שופר plated with gold
steps.stepSummary: Gold plating on the inside makes the שופר פסול. Plating on the outside makes it פסול only if it changes the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he plated it with gold on the inside, it is פסול. On the outside: if its sound changed from what it was, it is פסול; if not, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא, which now discusses a שופר covered with gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside plating means the air and sound pass over gold, not horn, so it is פסול no matter what. Outside plating does not touch the air path. It is judged only by whether the sound stays the same.

phrases.english: If he plated it with gold on the inside, it is unfit.
On the outside: if its sound changed
from what it was, it is unfit,
and if not, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 16 with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside gold plating makes the שופר פסול. Outside plating makes it פסול only if it changes the sound.

steps.title: A cracked שופר: lengthwise vs. across
steps.stepSummary: A lengthwise crack makes the שופר פסול. A crack across its width is fine if enough length for blowing remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it cracked along its length, it is פסול. If across its width: if a blowing-size piece remains, it is כשר; if not, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the case of a שופר that has a crack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lengthwise crack disqualifies the שופר outright, whatever its length, because blowing tends to spread it along the horn. A crack across the width damages only one spot. The usable part is then the section by the mouthpiece, before the crack, and it must still be the minimum blowing size.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum size needed to blow

phrases.english: If it cracked along its length, it is unfit.
Across its width: if there remains in it
the measure for blowing, it is fit,
and if not, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lengthwise crack makes the שופר פסול. A widthwise crack is כשר if a שיעור תקיעה remains.

steps.title: How long is the minimum blowing size?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how much the minimum blowing size is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the measure for blowing?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question about the term it just used. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crack rule depends on 'שיעור תקיעה', but no number was given yet. This question asks for that size.

phrases.english: And how much is the measure for blowing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term used in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical size of a שיעור תקיעה.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: visible on both sides of the hand
steps.stepSummary: The שופר must be long enough that, held in a fist, it sticks out on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explained: enough that he holds it in his hand and it can be seen on this side and that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is a little more than a handbreadth (טפח). Holding it in a closed fist, some of the שופר must show past the hand on each side.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds it in his hand
On this side and on that side

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
Enough that he can hold it in his hand
and it can be seen on this side and on that side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Long enough to stick out on both sides of a closed hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard practical measure for the minimum length of a שופר.

steps.title: Every kind of שופר sound is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: A thin, thick, or hoarse sound is כשר, because all sounds of a שופר are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its sound was thin, thick, or dry, it is כשר, because all sounds are כשר in a שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a rule about the quality of the שופר's sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the sound of a שופר but no particular tone. So an unusual sound does not disqualify it. This differs from the gold-plating case, where the problem was a sound that changed because of something added.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict Step 22. There the sound changed because of gold, an outside material, so it was no longer a pure שופר sound. Here the שופר's own natural sound is simply unusual.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rules: inside gold plating is פסול, and outside plating is פסול only if the sound changes. A lengthwise crack is פסול, and a widthwise crack is כשר if a hand's-width-plus remains. Every natural שופר sound is כשר.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה קוֹלוֹ דַּק אוֹ עָבֶה אוֹ צָרוּר — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: If its sound was thin, or thick, or dry, it is fit,
because all sounds are fit in a shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה קוֹלוֹ דַּק אוֹ עָבֶה אוֹ צָרוּר — כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any natural sound of a שופר, thin, thick, or hoarse, is כשר.

steps.title: Ruling sent to שמואל's father: a drilled horn is כשר
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent to אבוה דשמואל: if one drilled out a horn and blew it, he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to שמואל's father: if he drilled it and blew with it, he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling sent from ארץ ישראל to שמואל's father about a drilled-out horn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horn has a bony core that must be removed to make it hollow. The ruling says a horn that was drilled out can be used for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent by letter)

phrases.english: They sent to Shmuel's father:
If he drilled it and blew with it, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about drilling a שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drilled-out horn is valid for blowing.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? Every שופר is drilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling as obvious, since all שופרות are drilled out anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! All the others are also drilled out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling to שמואל's father: why say something so obvious? It is setting up an explanation of what the ruling really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every horn must have its bony core removed to become a שופר. So 'a drilled horn is כשר' seems to teach nothing new. The question pushes us to find a specific case the ruling must be talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a ruling teaches nothing new)

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא does not reject the ruling. It is not saying the ruling is wrong, only that it seems too obvious to need saying. The answer will show what new case it teaches.

phrases.english: It is obvious,
aren't all of them also drilled out?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי מִיקְדָּח קָדְחוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 27 as stating the obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling sent to אבוה דשמואל that a drilled horn is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every שופר is drilled to remove its bony core, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The horn was drilled through its bony core
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ruling is about drilling through the bony core (זכרות) rather than removing it. It teaches that same-material bone does not block the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the case is where he drilled through the bony core. You might have said that something of the same material still counts as a barrier, so the ruling teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from Step 28 by showing the ruling is not obvious after all. The case is a special one where the bony core was drilled through and left in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal שופר has its bony core pulled out completely. Here the person drilled a hole through the bone, so the sound passes through bone that is still inside the horn. We might have thought this bone is a barrier (חציצה) between the person and the horn. The ruling teaches that bone from the same animal horn is מין במינו and does not count as a barrier.

keyTerms.meaning: He drilled it out (bored a hole through it)
Its bony core, the bone inside the animal's horn
You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Same type with same type (same material)
It teaches us (the real point of the ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 28 said 'all horns are drilled out.' That means the core is normally removed. Here the core was drilled through and left inside, so the case is different.
steps.whatToRemember: A שופר drilled through its own bony core is כשר, because same-material bone is not a barrier (מין במינו אינו חוצץ).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: where he drilled it through its bony core.
phrases.notes: Instead of removing the bone, he bored through it.

phrases.english: You might have said: same material with same material does interpose,
phrases.notes: The mistaken assumption: the bone blocks the horn.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: Same material is not a barrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 28 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so the ruling teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bone of the same horn left inside would be a barrier (מין במינו חוצץ), making the שופר פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Same-material bone is not a barrier, so he is יוצא.

steps.title: Only listeners at the edge of the pit miss the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about blowing into a pit or cistern. רב הונא limits it: only people standing at the edge are not יוצא, while people inside the pit are יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one who blows into a pit or a cistern, etc. רב הונא said: this was taught only about those standing at the edge of the pit, but those standing inside the pit have fulfilled their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of blowing into a pit. רב הונא then narrows who fails to be יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People standing at the edge, outside the pit, hear the echo coming up from the pit. They do not hear the real שופר sound, so they are not יוצא. People inside the pit hear the actual sound of the שופר first, so they are יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit dug in the ground
They only taught this about... (limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Standing in the pit' and 'standing at the edge' describe the listeners, not the person blowing. The question is who hears the real sound and who hears only an echo.

phrases.english: One who blows into a pit
or into a cistern, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: he is not יוצא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: they taught this only
about those standing at the edge of the pit,
but those standing in the pit have fulfilled their obligation.
phrases.notes: They hear the real שופר sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the drilled שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing into a pit fails only for listeners outside at the edge. Listeners inside the pit are יוצא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the blower is יוצא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says one who blows into a pit or cistern is יוצא, as support for רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: one who blows into a pit or into a cistern has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building a proof for רב הונא by quoting a ברייתא. This is the setup; the next steps show how the ברייתא proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules the opposite of the משנה's plain words: it says 'יצא.' On its own, this looks like a clash. It becomes support for רב הונא once we see that only his split can fit both sources.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who blows into a pit
or into a cistern has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: The opposite wording from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רב הונא's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's split between listeners at the edge and listeners in the pit
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling יצא for blowing into a pit

steps.title: But the משנה says he is not יוצא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא clashes with the משנה, which says לא יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: he has not fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא highlights the clash between the ברייתא and the משנה. This is the middle of the proof, setting up the conclusion that only רב הונא's split resolves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'לא יצא' and the ברייתא says 'יצא' about the same case. Something must explain the difference. Pointing out the clash is what turns the ברייתא into proof for רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה: he has not fulfilled his obligation!
phrases.notes: The two sources seem to contradict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ברייתא contradicts the משנה, as part of building the proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules לא יצא in the identical case, so the two sources clash.

steps.title: So the ברייתא proves רב הונא right
steps.stepSummary: The only way to fit both sources is רב הונא's split, so the ברייתא proves his view. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it clear from this that the sources follow רב הונא? Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the contradiction is resolved only by רב הונא's distinction, which proves him right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (יצא) must be about listeners inside the pit, and the משנה (לא יצא) must be about listeners at the edge. Since this split resolves the clash, the ברייתא counts as support for רב הונא. 'שמע מינה' at the end confirms the proof is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that...? (leads into a proof)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (לא יצא) is about listeners at the edge who hear an echo. The ברייתא (יצא) is about listeners inside the pit who hear the real sound.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this that it is like Rav Huna,
phrases.notes: Only his split fits both sources.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash from Step 32 using רב הונא, completing the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא's distinction is proven by the ברייתא.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה and ברייתא contradict
steps.stepSummary: Some present this material differently, as a contradiction between the משנה (לא יצא) and the ברייתא (יצא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise them as a contradiction. We learned in the משנה: one who blows into a pit or a cistern has not fulfilled his obligation. But a ברייתא teaches: he has fulfilled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same discussion. In this version, the משנה and ברייתא are set against each other as a problem, and an answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources are the same as before, but the structure changes. In the first version, רב הונא spoke first and the ברייתא proved him. Here the contradiction comes first, and רב הונא's distinction is the answer to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some raise them as a contradiction (another version of the discussion)

phrases.english: There are those who raise them as a contradiction.
phrases.notes: A second version of the discussion.

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה: one who blows into a pit
or into a cistern has not fulfilled his obligation.
But a ברייתא teaches: he has fulfilled it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the same sources in a different format, as a contradiction instead of a proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling of לא יצא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules יצא in the identical case.

steps.title: רב הונא resolves it: edge versus inside the pit
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה refers to listeners at the edge of the pit, and the ברייתא refers to listeners inside the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: it is not difficult. Here the משנה is about those standing at the edge of the pit, and there the ברייתא is about those standing in the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction from Step 34 by assigning each source to a different group of listeners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are correct, but about different people. Listeners at the edge hear an echo, so they are not יוצא, as the משנה says. Listeners inside hear the real שופר sound, so they are יוצא, as the ברייתא says. The halacha comes out the same as in the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Here... there (each source refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions reach the same halacha. Hearing the echo from outside the pit is not enough, but hearing the actual שופר sound inside the pit is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the principle that a person must hear the real sound of the שופר. An echo (קול הברה) does not count.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: it is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִין עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר,
phrases.english: here (the משנה) is about those standing at the edge of the pit,
phrases.notes: Not יוצא, because they hear an echo.

phrases.english: there (the ברייתא) is about those standing in the pit.
phrases.notes: יוצא, because they hear the real sound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about listeners at the edge (an echo, not יוצא). The ברייתא is about listeners in the pit (the real sound, יוצא).

steps.title: רבה begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new teaching from רבה. This line only names the speaker. What he says comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by telling us that רבה is about to speak. The actual teaching has not arrived yet, so just note who is talking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אָמַר רַבָּה' are an attribution formula. They mark the start of an independent statement by an אמורא, not a reply to a question. Normally this line would be joined to the statement it introduces. Here this passage ends right after it, so it stands alone as an opening.

keyTerms.meaning: "Said." The standard word that opens a teaching quoted in someone's name.
רבה (בר נחמני), a leading אמורא of Babylonia. Do not confuse him with רָבָא.

steps.confusionAlert: רַבָּה (with a ה at the end) and רָבָא (with an א at the end) are two different אמוראים. Read the spelling carefully.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
phrases.notes: Attribution formula. The content of רבה's statement continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup / attribution line for an upcoming מימרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pit discussion was settled with רב הונא's split (steps 33–35), the גמרא turns to a fresh statement by רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated on this amud. Only the speaker, רבה, is introduced. His ruling follows on the next amud.
